title: 下终南山过斛斯山人宿置酒
title_en: Coming Down Zhongnan Mountain, I Stay the Night with the Hermit Husi, Who Sets Out Wine
author: 李白

readings.zh: “行衣”是走路时穿的衣服，读 xíng。
readings.en: Xíng yī means the clothes one walks in, so it is read xíng.

readings.zh: 这里是“歌曲”的意思，读 qǔ。
readings.en: Here it means a song, so it is read qǔ.

readings.zh: 这里是“快乐”的意思，读 lè。
readings.en: Here it means happy, so it is read lè.

glosses.zh: 碧山：青绿色的山，指终南山。终南山在长安南边。
glosses.en: bì shān: the green mountain, meaning Zhongnan Mountain, south of Chang'an.

glosses.zh: 苍苍：深青色，暮色中模模糊糊的样子。
glosses.en: cāng cāng: dark green, dim in the evening light.

glosses.zh: 翠微：青翠的山腰，也指青山。
glosses.en: cuì wēi: the green slopes of a mountain.

glosses.zh: 相携：手拉着手。指斛斯山人来接他，两人一起走。斛斯是姓，山人是住在山里的隐士。
glosses.en: xiāng xié: hand in hand. The hermit Husi meets him and they walk together. Husi is a surname; a "mountain man" is a hermit living in the hills.
jīng fēi: a gate woven from thorny branches, a simple farm gate.
yōu jìng: a quiet, shady path.

glosses.zh: 青萝：一种攀在树上垂下来的绿色植物。
glosses.en: qīng luó: a green vine that hangs down from trees.

glosses.zh: 得所憩：找到了休息的地方。憩，休息。
glosses.en: dé suǒ qì: to find a place to rest.

glosses.zh: 聊共挥：一起畅快地喝。聊，姑且；挥，举杯喝酒。
glosses.en: liáo gòng huī: to drink freely together. Huī here means raising the cup.

glosses.zh: 松风：一说指古琴曲《风入松》，一说指松林里的风声。
glosses.en: sōng fēng: one view is that it is the zither tune "Wind in the Pines"; another, that it is the sound of wind in the pines.

glosses.zh: 河星稀：天上银河里的星星变少了，说明夜已经很深，天快亮了。
glosses.en: hé xīng xī: the stars of the Milky Way grow few, so it is very late and nearly dawn.
táo rán: happy and at ease.

glosses.zh: 忘机：忘掉心机，不再算计世上的得失。
glosses.en: wàng jī: to forget all scheming and stop worrying about gain and loss.

translation.zh: 傍晚我从青翠的终南山上下来，
translation.en: At dusk I come down from the green mountain,

translation.zh: 山上的月亮一路跟着我回来。
translation.en: and the mountain moon follows me home.
I look back at the path I came by:

translation.zh: 只见青苍苍的暮色笼罩着山腰。
translation.en: dark green dusk lies across the slopes.

translation.zh: 斛斯山人拉着我的手来到他家，
translation.en: The hermit takes my hand and leads me to his farmhouse,
and the children run to open the wooden gate.
Green bamboo lines the quiet path,

translation.zh: 青萝轻轻擦过我的衣裳。
translation.en: and green vines brush my clothes.

translation.zh: 我高兴地说，找到了歇脚的好地方，
translation.en: I say happily that I have found a good place to rest,

translation.zh: 我们一起举杯，畅快地喝美酒。
translation.en: and we raise our cups of fine wine together.
We sing out loud the song of wind in the pines,

translation.zh: 歌唱完了，银河里的星星已经稀稀落落。
translation.en: and when the song ends, the stars of the Milky Way are few.
I am drunk, and you are happy too;

translation.zh: 我们开开心心，把世上的心机全忘了。
translation.en: in our joy we both forget the schemes of the world.

background.zh: 终南山在长安南边，山里住着不少隐士。这首诗写李白有一天傍晚从终南山下来，到一位姓斛斯的隐士家里住了一夜，两人喝酒唱歌到深夜。斛斯山人的名字和生平都没有记载。一说这首诗写于李白在长安的那几年。
background.en: Zhongnan Mountain lies south of Chang'an, and many hermits lived there. In this poem Li Bai comes down the mountain one evening and spends the night at the home of a hermit surnamed Husi. They drink and sing late into the night. Nothing is recorded about the hermit's full name or life. One view is that the poem dates from Li Bai's years in Chang'an.

author_note.zh: 李白（701—762），唐代大诗人，人称“诗仙”。他喜欢游山玩水，爱喝酒，也爱和隐士交朋友。他的诗多半奔放豪迈，这首却写得很安静、很亲切，有点像陶渊明写田园生活的味道。
author_note.en: Li Bai (701–762) was a great Tang poet, called the Immortal of Poetry. He loved travelling in the hills, loved wine, and liked making friends with hermits. Most of his poems are bold and sweeping, but this one is quiet and warm. It feels a little like Tao Yuanming's poems about country life.

appreciation.zh: 诗像一段小小的旅行日记。开头写下山：月亮跟着人走，好像也舍不得离开。回头看，山已经被暮色染成一片青苍。到了朋友家，孩子开门，竹林夹路，藤萝碰着衣服，一切都那么亲切。然后就是喝酒、唱歌，一直到星星都稀了。最后两句最动人：我醉了，你也乐了，我们都忘了世上那些算计。读这首诗，好像能闻到竹林的清香，听到松风的声音，感到朋友之间那份简单的快乐。
appreciation.en: The poem is like a little travel diary. It starts with coming down the mountain. The moon follows him, as if it does not want to leave either. Looking back, he sees the mountain turned dark green by the dusk. At his friend's house the children open the gate, bamboo lines the path, and vines brush his clothes. Everything feels warm and welcoming. Then they drink and sing until the stars grow few. The last two lines touch the heart most: I am drunk, you are happy, and we both forget the scheming of the world. Reading it, you can almost smell the bamboo, hear the wind in the pines, and feel the simple joy between two friends.
